title: I2C Conversation Animator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: I2C
Communication Buses
Device Addressing
Acknowledge Bit
description: Step through one I2C write transaction - START, address and write bit, ACK, data byte, ACK, STOP - and see the SDA and SCL waveforms for each part.

learningObjectives: Describe the order of an I2C write: START, address + W, ACK, data, ACK, STOP
Explain how the address lets only one device respond on a shared bus
Identify a missing ACK as the sign of a wrong address or a wiring fault
prerequisites: The SDA and SCL lines and device addresses (Chapter 8)

keyQuestions: Why does SDA only change while SCL is low?
Who pulls SDA low during an ACK?
What does the controller do when no device answers?
commonMisconceptions: Every device answers every message (only the device with the matching address sends ACK)
The ACK is sent by the Pico (the receiving device sends it)
assessmentOpportunities: The student converts 0x68 to the seven bits 1101000 and finds them on the waveform.
The student explains that the device, not the Pico, drives the ACK bit.
The student links a NACK to an OSError and a wiring or address problem.

controls.label: Talk to
controls.description: Chooses the OLED (0x3C), RTC (0x68), sensor (0x76) or a wrong address (0x50)

controls.label: data
controls.description: Chooses the data byte to send

controls.label: Next step
controls.description: Adds the next part of the transaction to the waveform
